title: Model Risk Management Policy
body:
Document owner: John Garcia, Credit Risk Analyst, Risk
Last updated: 2026-08-04
Applies to: Trading, Wealth Management, Lending, M&A Advisory, Compliance, Risk, Operations, Technology

Purpose
This policy sets out how Halcyon Ridge Capital identifies, validates, approves, monitors and retires quantitative models. A model is any method that applies statistical, economic, financial or machine-learning techniques to turn inputs into estimates that inform a business or control decision. The goal is to ensure that model outputs are fit for purpose and that the limits of each model are understood by the people relying on it.

Scope
The policy covers models in production and models in development, including vendor models and spreadsheets that meet the definition above. Examples include the intraday VaR and exposure calculations in RiskEngine, instrument valuation logic in PricingSvc, the credit decisioning models in CreditScoring, the fraud models in FraudScore, the transaction monitoring scenarios in AMLMonitor, and the rebalancing logic in PortfolioMgr. Simple arithmetic tools, reports and dashboards in ReportingBI are out of scope unless they embed a model.

Roles and Responsibilities
Model Owner: the business lead accountable for a model. For example, the Head of Lending owns CreditScoring models and the Head of Risk owns RiskEngine methodology. Owners must keep documentation current and attest annually.
Model Developer: the quant analyst, data engineer or software engineer who builds and changes the model. Trading quants and Technology engineers act as developers for most pricing and risk models.
Model Validator: a member of the Risk team independent of the developer and owner. Credit Risk Analysts validate credit models; the Market Risk Manager coordinates validation of market and pricing models.
Model Risk Committee: chaired by the Head of Risk, with the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer and Chief Compliance Officer as members. It approves tiering, accepts residual risk and signs off on exceptions.
Compliance: reviews models that support sanctions, KYC, fraud and AML controls for regulatory fit, in partnership with the Compliance Engineering Lead.

Model Inventory and Tiering
Risk maintains the model inventory. Every model must be registered before it is used in production. Each model is assigned a tier:
Tier 1: high impact on capital, P&L, credit decisions or regulatory obligations. Examples are RiskEngine VaR, PricingSvc valuation and the AML and fraud models. Full independent validation is required before use and annually thereafter.
Tier 2: moderate impact. Validation is proportionate and refreshed every two years or on material change.
Tier 3: low impact. Owner self-assessment with a Risk review of documentation.
Tiering considers materiality, complexity, data quality, reliance on upstream systems and the degree of human override.

Development Standards
Developers must document the purpose, theory, assumptions, data sources, known limitations, and intended use. Inputs must be traceable. Where a model depends on another system, such as pricing models consuming MarketDataFeed through PricingSvc or credit models reading from DataLake, the dependency and its data quality controls must be written down. Code must be version controlled, peer reviewed and reproducible in a non-production environment.

Validation
Independent validation covers conceptual soundness, data integrity, implementation testing, outcome analysis and sensitivity or stress testing. For Tier 1 models, validators must also perform benchmarking against an alternative approach where feasible and backtesting against realized outcomes. Findings are rated high, medium or low. High findings block production approval unless the Model Risk Committee grants a time-limited exception. Validators issue a written report within 30 business days of receiving a complete package.

Change Management
Material changes require revalidation before release. Material changes include new methodology, new data sources, recalibration beyond agreed tolerances, and changes in intended use. Technology releases touching model code follow the standard change process in #it-ops, and the validator confirms sign-off before deployment. Emergency fixes may be deployed with Head of Risk approval but must be validated within 15 business days.

Ongoing Monitoring
Owners monitor performance against defined thresholds, such as VaR backtesting exceptions, score drift in credit models, and alert-to-case conversion rates in AML scenarios. Breaches are escalated to Risk within two business days. Persistent breaches trigger a review and, if needed, a restriction or retirement of the model. Monitoring results are summarized quarterly for the Model Risk Committee.

Model Overrides and Use Restrictions
Users may override model outputs only with documented rationale and approval from the model owner. Override frequency is tracked and reviewed. Models must not be used outside their approved scope.

Vendor Models
Vendor models receive the same tiering. Where source code is unavailable, validation focuses on outcome analysis, vendor documentation, and controls over inputs. Vendor changes must be notified to Risk.

Issue Management and Retirement
Findings are tracked to closure with owners and due dates. Models that are no longer used must be retired, with the inventory updated and archived documentation retained according to the firm's records policy.

Policy Review
This policy is reviewed annually by Risk and approved by the Model Risk Committee. Questions should be sent to the Risk team or posted in #risk.
